title: One of the Greatest Sports Broadcasters of All Time
author: Admired Leadership
summary: Written on the occasion of Vin Scully's death, this piece uses the legendary Dodgers broadcaster's career as a leadership case study in humility. Scully's gift wasn't just his voice or storytelling, the author argues, but his deliberate refusal to make broadcasts about himself, even as he became one of the most beloved voices in sports history. The article traces examples of Scully self-effacing his own judgment, deflecting attention from himself toward players and fans, and being visibly uncomfortable when honored. The piece closes by generalizing the lesson to leadership broadly: humility isn't thinking less of yourself, but talking about yourself less.
points: Vin Scully's popularity stemmed as much from his humility as from his broadcasting skill.
He consistently redirected attention and credit toward players rather than himself.
Even self-deprecating anecdotes (like underestimating Sandy Koufax) reinforced his humble persona.
Players' tribute in his final broadcast caught him by surprise, underscoring his lack of self-regard.
The article generalizes: humility in leadership means speaking about yourself less, not thinking less of yourself.
quotes: Described as the “soundtrack of summer,” Scully broadcasted for the Dodgers baseball team for 67 years
What made him so great? Scully had a distinctive and soothing voice and combined that quality with a curiosity
In a game full of status and privilege, Scully never sought out attention for himself.
I always wanted to make sure I could push the game and players rather than me,
What a scout I am, he told everyone for decades, as Koufax became the most prolific pitcher in Dodgers' history.
It took Scully more than an inning to notice. He was bewildered by why they thought so highly of him.
You and I have been friends for a long time. But I know in my heart that I’ve always needed you more than you’ve ever needed me.
For Vin Scully, like so many great leaders, humility was not about thinking less about himself.
